3. DESIGN
3.1 Workflow Diagram and Explanation
Fig 3.1: Workflow of the E-Commerce website
• Home Page: The user lands on the home page showing featured products, categories and offers.
• Register / Login: New users create an account; existing users log in. Details are validated before
access is given.
• Browse Products: Products are listed by category, with search and filter options (price, category).
• Product Details: Shows image, price, description and the Add to Cart button.
• Cart: Selected items are stored in the cart. The user can change quantity, remove items and see
the total.
• Checkout and Payment: The user enters the delivery address and selects a payment method.

4. IMPORTANT CODE AND EXPLANATION
The sample code below shows the key modules of the website (HTML, CSS and JavaScript).
Replace or adjust it to match your own project files.
4.1 Product Card Layout (HTML)
<div class="product-card">
<img src="images/shoe.jpg" alt="Running Shoe">
<h3>Running Shoe</h3>
<p class="price">Rs. 1,499</p>
<button onclick="addToCart(1)">Add to Cart</button>
</div>
Explanation: Each product is shown as a card with image, name, price and button. The button calls
addToCart() with the product ID.
4.2 Responsive Grid (CSS)
.product-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns:
repeat(auto-fill, minmax(220px, 1fr)); gap: 20px; }
@media (max-width: 600px) {
.product-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
}
Explanation: CSS Grid arranges the cards automatically; the media query shows one column on
mobile screens, making the site responsive.
4.3 Add to Cart using localStorage (JavaScript)
function addToCart(id) { let cart =
JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cart")) || []; const
item = cart.find(p => p.id === id); if (item) item.qty
+= 1; else cart.push({ id: id, qty: 1 });
localStorage.setItem("cart", JSON.stringify(cart));
updateCartCount(); }
Explanation: The cart is read from localStorage. If the product exists, its quantity increases;
otherwise it is added. The updated cart is saved back, so it remains after page refresh.
4.4 Cart Total Calculation
function getTotal(products) { const cart =
JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("cart")) || []; return
cart.reduce((sum, c) => { const p = products.find(x =>
x.id === c.id); return sum + p.price * c.qty; }, 0);
}
Explanation: reduce() multiplies each item price by its quantity and adds them to give the cart
total.
4.5 Login Form Validation
document.getElementById("loginForm").addEventListener("submit", e => {
e.preventDefault(); const email =
document.getElementById("email").value.trim(); const pass =
document.getElementById("password").value;
if (!/^\S+@\S+\.\S+$/.test(email) || pass.length < 6) {
alert("Enter a valid email and a password of 6+ characters");
return; } window.location.href = "index.html"; });
Explanation: The form is stopped from submitting until the email format and password length are
checked. Valid users are redirected to the home page.

5. HOSTING DETAILS
The website was hosted using GitHub Pages, which gives free static hosting directly from a GitHub
repository.
Hosting Platform GitHub Pages
Repository Name ______________________
Live URL https://<username>.github.io/<repo-name>/
Repository URL https://github.com/<username>/<repo-name>
Steps followed
1. Create a new repository on GitHub (public).
2. Upload the project files (index.html, CSS, JS, images) or push using Git: git init, git add .,
git commit -m "first commit", git push origin main.
3. Open Settings > Pages, choose the main branch and / (root) folder, then click Save.
4. Wait 1-2 minutes; GitHub shows the live URL of the website.
5. Open the URL and test all pages after hosting.

6.CHALLENGES FACED
No.
Challenge
How it was solved
1
Responsive design
Layout broke on small screens. Solved with CSS Grid,
Flexbox and media queries.
2
Cart data lost on refresh
Cart items disappeared after reloading. Solved by storing
the cart in localStorage.
3
Form validation
Invalid emails and empty fields were being accepted.
Solved with JavaScript validation and regular expressions.
4
Image and file paths after
hosting
Images did not load on GitHub Pages because of wrong
paths and case-sensitive file names. Fixed with relative
paths and consistent naming.
5
Cross-browser differences
Some styles looked different in different browsers. Tested
in Chrome, Edge and Firefox and adjusted the CSS.
6
Git and deployment errors
Faced push and branch errors at first. Learned the basic
Git workflow (add, commit, push) to resolve them.
7.CONCLUSION
The E-Commerce website was designed and developed to let users browse products, add them to a
cart, and complete the checkout process through a simple, responsive interface. The project gave
practical experience with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, form validation, client-side data storage,
version control with Git, and deployment on GitHub Pages.
Future enhancements: a back-end with a database (Node.js / MongoDB), secure authentication, a
real payment gateway, an admin dashboard, and product reviews and ratings.
